---

The official Go library for the Tungo Platform API (`https://api.tungo.kz`): the AI accountant, 1C integration, bank statements, e-invoices, tax forms and automations of [Tungo AI](https://tungo.kz).

It is generated from the API's OpenAPI contract, so its methods and models always match the contract it was built from.

## Requirements

Go 1.24 or newer. The module has no dependencies outside the standard library. CI tests it on Go 1.24 and on the current stable release, with the race detector.

## Installation

```sh
go get github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-go@latest
```

```go
import tungo "github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-go"
```

## Quick start

```go
// Command quickstart asks the accountant one question and prints the answer.
//
//	TUNGO_API_KEY=tg_... TUNGO_COMPANY_ID=co_... go run ./examples/quickstart
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"

	tungo "github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-go"
)

func main() {
	// NewClient reads TUNGO_API_KEY, TUNGO_COMPANY_ID and TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID from the environment.
	client := tungo.NewClient()

	turn, err := client.Ask(context.Background(), "Сколько денег на расчётном счёте?")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Println(turn.Answer)
}
```

## Authentication and configuration

Create one client and share it: it is immutable and safe to use from several threads or tasks. Every option can be passed explicitly; five of them fall back to environment variables.

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `TUNGO_API_KEY` | none |
| Base URL | `TUNGO_BASE_URL` | `https://api.tungo.kz` |
| Webhook secret | `TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | none |
| Default company | `TUNGO_COMPANY_ID` | none |
| Default workspace | `TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID` | none |
| Timeout | | 60 s (600 s for non-streaming chat turns) |
| Maximum retries | | 2 |
| Default headers, HTTP client | | none, built-in |

The API key is sent only to operations that require it; public endpoints and incoming hooks never receive it, and it never appears in error messages or debug output. Calling an authenticated operation without a key fails locally, before any request is made.

Every method also accepts per-request options: timeout, maximum retries, extra headers, an idempotency key and cancellation.

```go
client := tungo.NewClient(
	tungo.WithAPIKey(os.Getenv("MY_TUNGO_KEY")),  // default (also when the value is empty): TUNGO_API_KEY
	tungo.WithCompanyID("co_123"),                // default: TUNGO_COMPANY_ID
	tungo.WithWorkspaceID("ws_123"),              // default: TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID
	tungo.WithBaseURL(os.Getenv("MY_TUNGO_URL")), // default (also when the value is empty): TUNGO_BASE_URL, then https://api.tungo.kz
	tungo.WithTimeout(30*time.Second),            // default: 60 s, 600 s for a chat turn
	tungo.WithMaxRetries(3),                      // default: 2
	tungo.WithHTTPClient(&http.Client{}),         // default: a shared client with keep-alive
	tungo.WithHeader("X-Trace", "billing-job"),
)

// Every option can also be passed to one call. The client itself never changes, so it is
// safe to share between goroutines.
var resp *tungo.Response
dialogs, err := client.Chat.List(ctx, &tungo.ChatListParams{Limit: tungo.Ptr(int64(20))},
	tungo.WithCompanyID("co_456"),
	tungo.WithResponseInto(&resp),
)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(len(dialogs.Data), "dialogs, request id", resp.RequestID())

// A client for another company that shares the connections of the first one.
other := client.WithOptions(tungo.WithCompanyID("co_789"))
```

The company (`co_...`) and the workspace (`ws_...`) are options too: `WithCompanyID` and `WithWorkspaceID`, with the environment variables `TUNGO_COMPANY_ID` and `TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID` as defaults. `WithAPIKey("")` and `WithBaseURL("")` are ignored, so an unset variable of your own leaves the defaults in force. Every method takes a `context.Context` first and `...tungo.Option` last. `fmt` never prints the key: `%+v` of a client shows `APIKey: [REDACTED]`. `WithMiddleware` wraps the HTTP round trip of every attempt (logging, tracing); `tungo.RedactHeaders` hides credentials in headers you log.

## Errors

Every failure is a subtype of the SDK's base error. An HTTP error response becomes an API error chosen by the `error.type` field of the response body, falling back to the HTTP status when the body is not the API's error envelope:

| `error.type` | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_request_error` | 400 |
| `authentication_error` | 401 |
| `payment_required_error` | 402 |
| `permission_error` | 403 |
| `not_found_error` | 404 |
| `conflict_error` | 409 |
| `gone_error` | 410 |
| `limit_error` | 429 |
| `api_error` | 500 |
| `unavailable_error` | 503 |

An API error carries the status, type, code, message, request id, field errors, the parsed retry-after delay, the response headers and the raw body. Problems that happen without a response have their own types: connection error, timeout, decode error (a successful response whose body is not valid), and configuration or validation error (raised before any request).

```go
_, err := client.Proposals.Get(ctx, "P-000042")

var apiErr *tungo.APIError
var timeoutErr *tungo.TimeoutError
var connErr *tungo.ConnectionError
switch {
case err == nil:
	// success
case errors.As(err, &apiErr):
	// The API answered with an error. Kind is the stable thing to branch on.
	switch apiErr.Kind {
	case tungo.KindNotFound:
		fmt.Println("no such proposal")
	case tungo.KindLimit:
		if apiErr.HasRetryAfter {
			fmt.Println("limit reached, try again in", apiErr.RetryAfter)
		}
	default:
		fmt.Println(apiErr.StatusCode, apiErr.Code, apiErr.Message, "request id:", apiErr.RequestID)
	}
case errors.As(err, &timeoutErr):
	fmt.Println("no answer within", timeoutErr.Limit)
case errors.As(err, &connErr):
	fmt.Println("could not reach the API:", connErr)
case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
	fmt.Println("cancelled by the caller")
default:
	return err // *tungo.DecodeError, *tungo.ConfigError, *tungo.ValidationError, ...
}

// When only the kind matters:
if tungo.KindOf(err) == tungo.KindAuthentication {
	fmt.Println("check TUNGO_API_KEY")
}
```

All SDK errors implement `tungo.Error` and work with `errors.As` and `errors.Is`: a `*TimeoutError` matches `context.DeadlineExceeded`, a cancelled call matches `context.Canceled`. `*APIError` also carries the typed `Detail` of the error envelope and `Extra` with the properties this SDK version does not know.

## Retries and timeouts

A request is retried up to 2 times (3 attempts) on connection errors, timeouts and the statuses 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, but only when repeating it is safe: `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT` and `DELETE` requests, and `POST` or `PATCH` requests of the operations whose contract declares an `Idempotency-Key`. For those the SDK generates a random key and reuses it for every attempt; you can pass your own. Other operations send no key, not even one you pass, because the API would ignore it.

The delay between attempts is `min(0.5 s × 2^attempt, 8 s)` with random jitter. A positive `retry-after-ms` or `Retry-After` response header overrides it; if the server asks for more than 60 s the SDK does not wait and raises the error with the delay filled in.

The timeout covers the whole request including reading the body. Streaming calls have no total timeout, only a connect timeout and an idle timeout of 120 s. Cancellation supplied by the caller is combined with the timeout.

```go
// For the whole client...
client := base.WithOptions(
	tungo.WithMaxRetries(5),           // 0 disables retries
	tungo.WithTimeout(20*time.Second), // for every attempt, the response body included
)

// ...or for one call.
account, err := client.Platform.GetAccount(ctx,
	tungo.WithMaxRetries(0),
	tungo.WithRequestTimeout(5*time.Second),
)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(account.BalanceTiyn)

// The deadline of the context bounds the call as a whole, retries and pauses included.
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Minute)
defer cancel()

// A POST is retried only with an Idempotency-Key. The SDK generates one for the operations
// that accept it and repeats it on every attempt; pass your own to make a retry of your
// whole job safe as well.
turn, err := client.Chat.Create(ctx,
	tungo.ChatMessageRequest{Message: tungo.Ptr("Проведи выписку за вчера")},
	tungo.WithIdempotencyKey("statement-2026-11-09"),
)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(turn.Answer)
```

`WithTimeout` and `WithRequestTimeout` bound one attempt. The SDK never sets `http.Client.Timeout`, so a custom HTTP client keeps working for streams. `WithStreamIdleTimeout` changes the idle timeout of streams; it counts only the time a read waits for the server, not the time your code spends on an event. A `Retry-After` of zero or in the past does not make the SDK retry at once: the normal backoff applies. The rate-limit headers of a response are available through `WithResponseInto` and `Response.RateLimit`.

## Pagination

List operations use cursor pagination (`{ data, next_cursor }`). The plain method returns one typed page that knows whether there is a next page and can fetch it. The auto-paging variant is a lazy iterator: it requests the next page only when needed, carries your filters over, and stops fetching as soon as you stop iterating.

```go
params := &tungo.ProposalsListParams{Status: tungo.Ptr("draft"), Limit: tungo.Ptr(int64(50))}

// One page at a time.
page, err := client.Proposals.List(ctx, params)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
for _, proposal := range page.Data {
	fmt.Println(proposal.ID, proposal.Total.Formatted)
}
if page.HasNext() {
	if page, err = page.Next(ctx); err != nil { // same filters, next cursor
		return err
	}
	fmt.Println(len(page.Data), "more")
}

// Or every item of every page. Pages are fetched as the loop needs them; break to stop.
for proposal, err := range client.Proposals.ListAll(ctx, params) {
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fmt.Println(proposal.ID)
}
```

The iterator ends with a `*tungo.PaginationError` if the API returns the same cursor twice, so a loop cannot spin forever.

## Streaming

Streaming operations use server-sent events and deliver typed events as they arrive. Leaving the loop early or closing the stream closes the connection. A stream request is retried only before its first byte; an error response is raised as the same typed API error as for ordinary calls. A chat stream that ends before its final event is reported as an error, never as a finished answer.

```go
stream, err := client.Chat.CreateStream(ctx, tungo.ChatMessageRequest{
	Message: tungo.Ptr("Что с НДС за квартал?"),
})
if err != nil {
	return err // a refused request is the same *tungo.APIError as for any other call
}
defer stream.Close() // not needed after a complete loop, harmless and safe on early return

for event, err := range stream.Events() {
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	switch e := event.Value.(type) {
	case *tungo.ChatEventText:
		fmt.Print(e.Delta)
	case *tungo.ChatEventTool:
		fmt.Printf("\n[%s: %s]\n", e.Name, e.Status)
	case *tungo.ChatEventDone:
		fmt.Println()
	case *tungo.UnknownVariant:
		// an event type added to the API after this SDK version: e.Tag, e.Raw
	}
}
fmt.Println("dialog:", stream.DialogID())

// When the pieces are not needed, let the SDK put the turn together.
stream, err = client.Chat.CreateStream(ctx, tungo.ChatMessageRequest{
	Message:  tungo.Ptr("А за прошлый?"),
	DialogID: tungo.Value(stream.DialogID()),
})
if err != nil {
	return err
}
turn, err := stream.Accumulate(nil)
if err != nil {
	return err // *tungo.TurnError when the turn itself failed
}
fmt.Println(turn.Text, turn.StopReason)
```

`Events` yields every event of the stream as a tagged union; an event type this SDK version does not know arrives as `*tungo.UnknownVariant` instead of failing the stream, and heart-beats are skipped. `RawEvents` yields the undecoded SSE events. `Accumulate` returns a `*tungo.TurnError` when the turn itself fails, and a `*tungo.DecodeError` that matches `tungo.ErrStreamIncomplete` when the stream ends before its `done` event: the text so far is then not a finished answer. A successful response that is not `text/event-stream` is a `*tungo.DecodeError` too. The exception is a finished chat turn that the API replays for a repeated `Idempotency-Key` (`application/json` with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`): its stored result arrives as the events of that turn, ending with `next` (follow-ups and the next action, when it has them) and `done`. The other streams (`Chat.ListEvents`, `Batches.ListEvents`, `Feed.ListEvents`) work the same way; after a broken connection, `LastEventID` tells where the stream stopped. The SDK does not reconnect on its own.

## Webhooks

Outgoing webhooks are signed according to the Standard Webhooks specification (Svix). The verify helper takes the raw request body and the headers (`webhook-*` or `svix-*`), checks the HMAC-SHA256 signature in constant time and the timestamp within 300 s of the system clock, and returns the typed event. Any problem is reported as a webhook verification error. If no secret is passed, the client's webhook secret is used.

The send-hook helper posts an event to an incoming hook (`/hooks/{token}`) and, when given a secret, signs the exact bytes it sends in the `X-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header. The API key is never sent to hooks.

```go
// Receiving: verify the bytes exactly as they arrived, before decoding anything.
body, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
// The secret (whsec_...) comes from WithWebhookSecret or TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Messages
// older or newer than five minutes are rejected; an empty secret is always an error.
event, err := client.VerifyWebhook(body, r.Header)
if err != nil {
	var verr *tungo.WebhookVerificationError
	if errors.As(err, &verr) {
		log.Println("rejected a webhook:", verr.Reason)
	}
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusBadRequest)
	return nil
}
switch e := event.Value.(type) {
case *tungo.WebhookEventProposalWritten:
	fmt.Println("written to 1C:", e.Data.ProposalID)
default:
	fmt.Println("event", event.Tag())
}
w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)

// Sending: start an automation through its hook. No API key is sent; the payload is signed
// with the hook secret, and the event id makes a repeated delivery harmless.
accepted, err := client.SendHook(ctx, "hk_token",
	map[string]any{"order_id": "A-17", "amount_tiyn": 1250000},
	&tungo.SendHookParams{Secret: os.Getenv("TUNGO_HOOK_SECRET"), EventID: "order-A-17"},
)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(accepted.EventID, accepted.Duplicate)
```

`tungo.VerifyWebhook(body, header, secret)` does the same without a client. `WithWebhookTolerance` changes the five-minute window. `tungo.SignHook` and `tungo.VerifyHookSignature` sign and check a hook payload by hand.

## Money

The API expresses amounts in tiyn (1/100 of a tenge) as 64-bit integers. The money helper converts decimal strings and exact decimal values to tiyn without floating-point error, rounding half away from zero (`"1.005"` → `101`), and formats tiyn for display (`4500000` → `45 000,00 ₸`). Invalid input raises a typed error.

```go
// The API counts money in tiyn (1 ₸ = 100 tiyn) as int64. Convert from decimal strings:
// they are exact, floats are not.
tiyn, err := tungo.ToTiyn("1234.50")
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(tiyn)                          // 123450
fmt.Println(tungo.FormatTiyn(tiyn, "KZT")) // 1 234,50 ₸
fmt.Println(tungo.TiynToDecimal(tiyn))     // 1234.50
fmt.Println(tungo.IsValidBINIIN("x"))      // false
half, _ := tungo.ToTiynFloat(0.285)        // floats are accepted and rounded half away from zero
fmt.Println(half)                          // 29
```

`ToTiynRat` converts an exact `*big.Rat`. `ToTiynFloat` exists for values that are already floats; prefer strings.

## Null, absent and zero values

Go's zero values cannot tell "not set" from "set to zero", so the models spell it out. In request types an optional property is a pointer (`nil`: not sent) and a property that accepts `null` is a `tungo.Nullable[T]` (zero value: not sent, `tungo.Null[T]()`: `null`, `tungo.Value(v)`: the value, even an empty list or zero). Required lists and maps are never sent as `null`. In responses a nullable or optional property is a pointer.

```go
// Optional fields are pointers: nil is "not sent", tungo.Ptr(false) is false.
// Fields the API accepts null for are tungo.Nullable: the zero value is "not sent".
_, err := client.Webhooks.UpdateEndpoint(ctx, "ep_1", tungo.WebhookEndpointPatch{
	Enabled:    tungo.Ptr(false),        // "enabled": false
	EventTypes: tungo.Value([]string{}), // "event_types": []
	Channels:   tungo.Null[[]string](),  // "channels": null
	// Description is not set: the property is not sent and stays as it is.
})
if err != nil {
	return err
}

// Responses keep what this SDK version does not know about.
endpoint, err := client.Webhooks.GetEndpoint(ctx, "ep_1")
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(endpoint.ExtraFields()) // properties added to the API later, as raw JSON
```

Every model keeps the JSON it was decoded from: `RawJSON()` returns it and `ExtraFields()` the properties this SDK version has no field for. Enums are string types, so a value added to the API later decodes without an error. A union with a discriminator is a struct with a `Value` holding one of its variant types (use a type switch); a union of plain JSON shapes is a struct with one pointer field per shape.

## Waiting for long operations

```go
// Start a scenario and wait until its run reaches a final state.
run, err := client.RunScenarioAndWait(ctx, "scn_1", nil, &tungo.WaitOptions{Timeout: 10 * time.Minute})
if err != nil {
	return err // *tungo.TimeoutError when the run is still going after ten minutes
}
fmt.Println(run.State)

// Upload a bank statement and wait for the batch that processes it.
statement := []byte("1CClientBankExchange\n...")
job, err := client.UploadBankStatement(ctx, "statement.txt", statement, true)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
if job, err = client.WaitForBatch(ctx, job.ID, nil); err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(job.Running) // false
```

The helpers poll with a pause that grows from 1 s to 5 s, stop on every final state of the contract, and honour the context. A poll that fails for a passing reason (a connection error, a timeout, 408, 429, 5xx) is repeated until the deadline; any other error ends the wait at once.

## API reference

Generated from the Tungo Platform API contract: **13 resources, 90 methods, 22 webhook event types**.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `client.Workspaces` | Organisations (workspaces) the API key can access | `List` |
| `client.Companies` | Companies of an organisation and their profiles | `List` · `Get` |
| `client.Platform` | Platform balance, ledger, usage reports, limits, audit log and model rates | `ListUsageRates` · `GetAccount` · `GetAudit / GetAuditAll` · `GetLedger / GetLedgerAll` · `ListLimits` · `ListRequests / ListRequestsAll` · `GetUsage` |
| `client.APIKeys` | The current API key and its usage statistics | `GetCurrent` · `GetCurrentUsage` · `GetUsage` |
| `client.Webhooks` | Outgoing webhooks of an organisation (Svix): endpoints, event catalogue, deliveries and signature check | `ListEndpoints / ListEndpointsAll` · `CreateEndpoint` · `GetEndpoint` · `UpdateEndpoint` · `DeleteEndpoint` · `ListEndpointAttempts / ListEndpointAttemptsAll` · `RotateEndpointSecret` · `TestEndpoint` · `ListEventTypes` · `ListMessages / ListMessagesAll` · `ListMessageAttempts / ListMessageAttemptsAll` · `ResendMessage` · `GetUsage` |
| `client.Chat` | Conversations with the AI accountant: questions, streaming chat (SSE), token counting and history | `List / ListAll` · `Create / CreateStream` · `CountTokens` · `ListMentions` · `GetRatingOptions` · `ListSuggestions` · `Get` · `Update` · `Delete` · `Answer / AnswerStream` · `ListEvents` · `RateMessage` · `DeleteMessageRating` · `Rate` · `DismissRating` · `Stop` |

| `client.ESF` | Incoming and outgoing electronic invoices (the ESF system) | `GetIncoming / GetIncomingAll` · `GetOutgoing / GetOutgoingAll` |
| `client.Forms` | Tax forms (FNO 100.00 and others): building, ISNA checks and data gaps | `List` · `Build` · `ListDataGaps` · `GetIsna` · `ListNotes` |
| `client.OneC` | Status of the company's connection to its 1C database | `GetStatus` |
| `client.Automations` | Company automations: incoming hooks, scenarios, step chains, runs and the AI autonomy level | `PostHook` · `ListHooks` · `CreateHook` · `GetHook` · `UpdateHook` · `DeleteHook` · `RotateHook` · `TestHook` · `ListRuns / ListRunsAll` · `GetRun` · `CancelRun` · `RetryRun` · `ListScenarios` · `CreateScenario` · `GetScenario` · `PutScenario` · `UpdateScenario` · `DeleteScenario` · `RunScenario` · `GetState` · `PutState` · `GetAutonomy` · `PutAutonomy` |

## Versioning and support

This library follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). While the major version is 0, a minor release may contain breaking changes; they are always listed in the [changelog](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-go/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). This README describes version 0.3.0.

The code is generated: please report problems and ideas in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-go/issues) rather than opening pull requests against generated files. To report a vulnerability, follow the [security policy](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-go/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
